title: Nested System Scan
description: Use nested WHILE loops to scan multiple ship decks and compartments.

story.setup: MENTOR-9: "The ship has 3 decks, and each deck has compartments. We need to scan all compartments on all decks. This requires nested WHILE loops—one for decks, one for compartments."
story.context: Nested loops are powerful for processing multi-dimensional data or hierarchical structures. The outer loop controls the major iteration (decks), while inner loops handle sub-iterations (compartments per deck).
story.success: MENTOR-9: "Excellent! You scanned all 3 decks and 4 compartments per deck—12 total scans. Nested WHILE loops let you handle complex, hierarchical tasks."

hints: Inner loop resets for each deck
Use indentation to show nesting clearly
Each WHILE needs its own END
Inner loop variable must be reset in outer loop
Use 2 spaces (  ) before compartment logs for visual hierarchy

theory.title: Exercise 3.1.5: Nested WHILE Loops
theory.content:
MENTOR-9: "Think of it like a grid. The outer loop moves down rows, the inner loop scans across columns. Each row starts the column scan fresh."

Nested WHILE Loops

A nested WHILE loop is a WHILE loop inside another WHILE loop:

WHILE    ${outer_condition}
    # Outer loop code
    WHILE    ${inner_condition}
        # Inner loop code
    END
    # More outer loop code
END

How It Works:

  1. Outer loop starts first iteration
  2. Inner loop runs all its iterations
  3. Outer loop continues to next iteration
  4. Inner loop runs again (reset)
  5. Process repeats

Example: 3x3 Grid Scan

${row}=    Set Variable    1
WHILE    ${row} <= 3
    ${col}=    Set Variable    1
    WHILE    ${col} <= 3
        Log    Position [${row},${col}]
        ${col}=    Set Variable    ${col + 1}
    END
    ${row}=    Set Variable    ${row + 1}
END

Output: Position [1,1], [1,2], [1,3], [2,1], [2,2], [2,3], [3,1], [3,2], [3,3]

⚠️ Nested Loop Tips

  • Inner loop variable MUST reset for each outer iteration
  • Each loop needs its own END
  • BREAK only exits the innermost loop
  • Use clear indentation (4 spaces per level)
  • Keep nesting shallow (2-3 levels max for readability)
